🖥 Pezzeshkian: European perceptions of Iran do not reflect reality

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian says perceptions of Iran held by some European countries do not accurately reflect the realities of the Islamic Republic, urging the new Danish ambassador to help present a more realistic image of the country.

Pezeshkian made the remarks during a ceremony on Tuesday to receive the credentials of Denmark’s new Ambassador to Iran, Christian Atzen.
​
“The mindset that has taken shape among some European countries toward Iran is not accurate and does not correspond to the realities of Iran,” the president said, expressing confidence that Atzen would be able to observe the realities of Iranian society, culture, and civilization firsthand during his mission and help correct such perceptions.
​
Pezeshkian highlighted Iran’s peaceful and engagement-oriented approach, saying the Iranian nation has historically pursued peace, tranquility, constructive relations, and healthy interaction with other countries.
​
“Denmark is also one of the countries with which Iran seeks to develop relations and interactions,” he added.
​
Atzen, for his part, expressed pleasure at beginning his mission in Iran and said he had been impressed by the country’s civilization, history and culture.
​
“I am happy to be in Iran and have been impressed by the beautiful civilization, history and unique culture of the Iranian people,” the Danish ambassador said.
​
He also pledged to convey a fair and accurate picture of Iran to Denmark. “I am committed to this and will carry it out with complete sincerity,” Atzen said.

🔊 Pezeshkian urges new ambassadors to carry message of brotherhood, unity

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has urged the country’s newly appointed ambassadors to promote brotherhood, friendship, and unity while defending national interests and expanding multilateral ties with their host countries.

Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday during a ceremony to introduce and bid farewell to Iran’s new ambassadors to the United Arab Emirates, Greece, Italy, Uganda, and Senegal.
​
“I hope you have a good journey ahead and properly carry out your missions in the direction of defending national interests and expanding multilateral relations, particularly in the economic field,” he said.
​
The president tasked the ambassadors with creating an environment conducive to strengthening multilateral relations and expanding scientific, cultural, economic, sports, and artistic exchanges with the countries.
​
Referring to Quranic verses and Islamic traditions, Pezeshkian highlighted the need for friendship and Islamic solidarity, calling on all countries to work to strengthen friendship and avoid tensions and disputes.
​
“Based on the verses and traditions, we are all Muslim countries and neighbors, members of one community and one hand; therefore, you dear ones should carry the message of brotherhood, friendship and unity,” he said.
​
Pezeshkian said stronger cooperation with regional and neighboring countries could pave the way for a joint Islamic parliament, which he said would contribute to the progress and development of Muslim societies and help establish security in the region.
​
He also described Islamic unity and solidarity as essential in the face of the hostilities of the Israeli regime, stressing the need to avoid religious disputes and expand Islamic cohesion across the region.
​
The new ambassadors introduced at the ceremony were Hamidreza Dehghani to the UAE, Mahmoud Heydari to Greece, Ali Akbar Rezaei to Italy, Reza Nourian to Uganda and Hamid Moradkhani to Senegal. They outlined their respective missions and strategies for expanding multilateral relations and cooperation.
